We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place.
